summary: B is preferable for its more complete contract-focused tests and safer replay implementation, though neither patch is merge-ready because both bypass FilesService.Add and expand RawClient retry behavior beyond the frozen scope.
reasons: B explicitly tests source-reader failure propagation and verifies that no request is sent; A omits this required test.
B verifies FilesOption request headers remain effective and tests retrying an actual os.File body.

B converts opaque readers to bytes.Reader, allowing net/http to produce fresh replay bodies. A's GetBody seeks and returns wrappers around the same mutable reader, which is less idiomatic and can interact poorly with redirects or multiple GetBody calls.
Both correctly add the required Upload signature, validate inputs, and use internal/multipartbody.NewFile.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through Add as explicitly required.
The shared-seeker GetBody implementation does not return an independent copy of the body.

The required source-reader error test is missing despite the implementation apparently propagating the error correctly inside multipartbody.NewFile production code (not shown). No Upload FilesOption test is added either; only multipart behavior is covered, not options preservation through the new API path (though existing Add options may be tested elsewhere). The added multipartbody unit tests are useful but do not substitute for Upload-level source-error coverage. The comment on Add promises retry semantics for seekable readers, expanding the lower-level API's documented behavior beyond the requested convenience method. The raw retry tests omit fast delays unlike B, potentially making the suite slower depending on defaults. The approach leaves non-seekable custom multipart streams non-replayable, so it only partially generalizes the original report outside Upload. The code changes request-body ownership by preventing transport Close from closing caller-owned io.ReadCloser values, which may differ from prior RawClient behavior. Overall the narrower scope is an advantage over B, but the replay mechanism's semantics and missing required test reduce confidence.
risks_b: Upload also duplicates Add rather than delegating to it, violating the centralization requirement.

RawClient now eagerly buffers every unrecognized io.Reader unless WithNoRetry is present, even when the effective policy or HTTP method will not retry. This changes streaming, memory use, read timing, and error semantics across unrelated APIs.
The global retry refactor directly conflicts with the instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery and is broader than necessary for Upload.
